key_insight: The paper argues that looped language models should be treated as fixed-point systems: once recurrent states get close to a stable point, the exact trajectory used to reach them matters much less. This unlocks cheaper training, decoding, distillation, and RL without major accuracy loss.
problem_solved: Looped models are computationally expensive because every extra recurrence increases cost in training, decoding, prefill, and reinforcement learning. The paper addresses how to reduce this overhead by exploiting near-fixed-point behavior.
method: Use truncated backpropagation during training when recurrent states are close to convergence.
Apply terminal KV sharing at decoding time to reuse final key-value states with minimal accuracy loss.
Distill a student model that leverages fixed-point behavior to speed up prefill up to 1.79x.
Compute RL gradients from saved rollout states instead of full backpropagation through the rollout, achieving about 2x speedup.
impact: This makes looped and recurrent LLMs far more practical by reducing compute cost across the full lifecycle of a model. Practitioners can gain faster training and inference while preserving most of the performance benefits of recurrence.
visual_elements: A looped model diagram showing states moving toward a fixed point.

paper_title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part II: Rethinking at Fixed Points
paper_authors: Benhao Huang, Chufan Shi, Junlin Chen, Shicheng Wen, Zhengzhong Liu
